mainText: Good morning. Here is your curated AI briefing for Tuesday, October 20, 2026. Researchers at security firm Claroc have discovered that Meta’s new general-purpose AI agent, Muse, can expose sensitive user information through its conversation-sharing feature. The vulnerability arises from how the platform generates URLs for shared chats. Although these links use long character strings intended to prevent guessing, the researchers found they could easily enumerate thousands of these links using passive DNS records—databases that track historical domain resolutions. By monitoring DNS responses, the firm successfully discovered 6,800 active links. In a test, they accessed private notes, loan applications, internal revenue reviews, and sensitive workplace data, including executive-search preparations and staff vacation calendars. The discovery highlights a significant security risk for enterprise users, as the feature allowed unauthorized third parties to view confidential business workflows without detection. Meta confirmed it is suspending the sharing feature while it reviews the design. The company maintains that the feature was intended for specific artifact sharing and notes it operates a bug bounty program to identify such vulnerabilities. In research developments, Hugging Face has released FairStress, a new benchmark designed to measure demographic fairness in large language models. While standard benchmarks typically test whether a model makes the same decision regardless of a subject’s demographic identity, FairStress goes further by testing the model’s resistance to persuasive pressure. Researchers found that models often exhibit "hidden asymmetries," where they are more or less likely to change an initial, fair-looking decision when presented with biased or adversarial arguments depending on which demographic group those arguments favor. FairStress evaluates models across 29 domains, including hiring, healthcare, and lending, aiming to promote a definition of fairness where a model’s well-supported decisions remain robust regardless of identity. By testing how easily models can be pushed away from evidence-based conclusions, this benchmark provides a deeper layer of accountability for developers building AI for high-stakes societal roles. In infrastructure news, Amazon Web Services has launched a generally available Model Context Protocol server for Smartsheet. This integration allows AI agents to interact with Smartsheet’s work management data—such as project timelines and task statuses—using natural language. By utilizing this standardized protocol, AI assistants can perform actions like updating project sheets or querying dependencies directly within tools like Amazon Quick or agentic integrated development environments like Kiro. The system is designed to provide token-efficient context by returning specific metadata rather than raw API payloads. AWS suggests this approach reduces operational costs and latency compared to processing raw data, making it more feasible to run hundreds of AI-assisted queries across a complex project portfolio. In the business sector, independent reporting from Bloomberg indicates that former Google CEO Eric Schmidt holds a stake in the AI lab Anthropic estimated at approximately 1 percent. This follows his investment in the company’s 2021 Series A round. Analysts suggest this is a significant position compared to the 2 percent stake held by Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei, particularly as the lab is widely expected to go public before the end of the year at a valuation that could reach $2 trillion. Additionally, OpenAI reported on internal usage metrics for ChatGPT Work, highlighting a case study in which a franchisee reduced the time required for monthly cash reconciliation by 94 percent, demonstrating the tangible labor-efficiency gains currently being realized by early enterprise adopters. Separately, NVIDIA announced that Spain’s Barcelona Supercomputing Center has expanded its AI Factory Accelerator Programme. The initiative, powered by NVIDIA hardware, provides startups with sovereign compute and technical resources. Several startups in the program are now utilizing these tools to develop applications in sectors ranging from water management and pharmaceutical sales to medical diagnostics.
